question: Should ClawHub enforce a 40-character skill display-name limit now, and should existing GitHub-backed over-limit names be preserved or intentionally migrated on next sync?
rationale: The PR chooses a public catalog limit and upgrade behavior for stored GitHub-backed rows, but the linked issue does not record maintainer approval for the exact limit or legacy handling.

options.title: Preserve legacy GitHub-backed names
options.body: Keep the 40-character new-name limit, but grandfather unchanged existing GitHub-backed over-limit display names the same way hosted publishes are grandfathered.

options.title: Accept sync migration
options.body: Allow the next GitHub sync to shorten existing over-limit names, but document that as intentional policy and add focused migration/proof coverage.

options.title: Pause for policy
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers settle the maximum length and legacy treatment in the linked issue.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy GitHub-backed names
recommendation.body: Keep the 40-character new-name limit, but grandfather unchanged existing GitHub-backed over-limit display names the same way hosted publishes are grandfathered.
